items.name: Guiding Data Allocation for Robust Subpopulation Generalization
items.title: Guiding Data Allocation for Robust Subpopulation Generalization
items.description: Machine learning models often achieve high average accuracy in the training data while performing poorly on test data due to subpopulation shift. A common data-centric solution is to enforce balanced subgroup proportions, but full balance can be costly, infeasible, and not always necessary. In this work, we study whether balanced training data is the unique optimal configuration for robust subpopulation generalization. items.title: Vendi Anomaly Scores for Efficient and Accurate Anomaly Detection
items.description: Anomaly detection (AD) is a critical for trustworthy machine learning and scientific discovery. items.title: Where Does Alignment Emerge and What Does It Mean? A Closer Look at the Platonic Representation Hypothesis
items.description: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) suggests that neural networks are converging toward similar representation spaces. As language models become more capable, their representations are aligning with those of vision models. However, recent work has questioned whether this trend continues to hold for newer language models. items.title: Shortcuts and Boundaries: Verifiable RL Misalignment and Contextual Safety Learning
items.description: Reinforcement learning (RL) can improve an agent's task capability while reinforcing behavior that violates contextual execution requirements. items.title: Is Persona Generalization Predictable?
items.description: Persona generalization occurs when fine-tuning a language model in one domain induces behavioral changes in others -- for example, the broadly unsafe behavior observed in emergent misalignment. items.title: WorkflowArena: Benchmarking Executable Workflow Orchestration in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
items.description: Large language model agents are increasingly deployed as multi-agent systems rather than as a standalone model operating within a single context. items.title: Mitigating Agentic Deception via Evaluation-Side Partially Observable Games
items.description: As large language models become more capable agents, they can exhibit deceptive behaviors, cheating human for higher rewards while appearing helpful. items.title: Programming Prescience: Issues in Human Construction of Forecasting Bots
items.description: AI models' growing capacity for complex reasoning has made them attractive tools for forecasting, or the systematic prediction of the future based on past and present data. items.title: What the Loss Curve Misses: FP4 Pretraining Slows the Acquisition of Rare Facts

items.title: How Well Does AI Peer Review Work? A Benchmark Built from 100 Planted Errors
items.description: One hundred known errors were planted into 10 open-access psychology papers, and the modified papers were then run through frontier models and two commercial AI review tools. The best single system caught 71 of the 100 errors, while the worst caught 30. Pooling every system's output caught 93. items.description: BACKGROUND: AI-based tools are expected to play a key role in lung cancer screening (LCS). items.description: Preference optimization has become a central approach for aligning large language models with human values, but its effectiveness depends heavily on the quality of preference annotations.
